name: Machir
title: Father of Geuel, the spy from the tribe of Gad
summary: Machir was the father of Geuel, who was chosen as the representative for the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies Moses sent into the land of Canaan. He is mentioned only in connection with his son's role in the spying mission. Although Machir himself did not play a prominent role, his son was part of the important event where the spies brought back a report from the promised land.

keyEvents.title: Geuel Chosen as a Spy
keyEvents.description: Machir's son Geuel was chosen to represent the tribe of Gad as one of the twelve spies sent to explore the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: The Spies Are Sent Out
keyEvents.description: Moses sent twelve men, including Geuel son of Machir, from the wilderness of Paran to spy out the land of Canaan by the Lord's command.

keyEvents.title: Return and Report of the Spies
keyEvents.description: After forty days of spying, the twelve spies returned with fruit from the land, but ten of them, likely including Geuel, gave a negative report that created fear among the people.

keyEvents.title: The People's Rebellion After the Spies' Report
keyEvents.description: The negative report from the majority of the spies led to the people of Israel rebelling against Moses and Aaron, and they refused to enter the promised land.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Unfaithful Spies
keyEvents.description: God judged the ten spies who brought the bad report, and they died by a plague before the Lord. Only Joshua and Caleb were spared.
